reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster. It incorporates a dedicated tempo run to build threshold strength, a crucial component for sustained speed on trails, alongside a longer, controlled endurance run. Plan B, while including some aerobic work, lacks this focused strength development and relies heavily on easy runs, which won't significantly improve speed. The inclusion of a strength session in Plan B is a positive, but it doesn't directly address the primary goal of increasing trail running speed.
